answer: A farm can mint keys in seconds, but it cannot cheaply keep one reachable service in one place for a month. Each applicant bonds a deposit and runs a single endpoint that five unaffiliated relays, scattered across the ocean, probe at random hours. Every reply carries a quartz timestamp and a path-delay signature; only a tight, unimodal fingerprint, stable for the whole month, unlocks voting and grading. The endpoint must also append a daily signed leaf to one continuous juniper log, so a cloned key that forks or goes dark slashes the whole cluster.
